summary: Octagonal red-brick light on Bogus Point, Lake Ontario, Hilton, New York: lit 17 August 1896, deactivated 1954, now a privately owned house.

lens.note: Original third-and-a-half-order Fresnel, from the Cleveland light's tower; USLHS: current optic removed.

structures.note: Heights conflict: 93 ft above MHW and 86 ft to lantern (USLHS); 97 ft original and 65 ft after 1995 (LF).

access.note: Privately owned; grounds, dwelling and tower closed (LF visitor note; USLHS: Open to Public: No).

visit.note: Privately owned; a public park (Bogus Point Park) lies just west of the lighthouse.

events.note: Congress appropriated $20,000 for the station (act of 3 March 1891)
New York ceded jurisdiction over the reservation under a general law of May 1892
Contract approved 25 June 1895 for keeper's dwelling, tower and wood shed (nine months)
Light first exhibited on the night of 17 August 1896
Third-and-a-half-order Fresnel lens, from the discontinued Cleveland light's tower
Lens replaced: 270-degree lens in place of a 180-degree lens
Main 3.5-order lens light discontinued 8 May to 30 June 1902 while the tower was repaired; a lens-lantern light was exhibited from the top of the tower instead
Illuminant changed from oil to incandescent oil vapor, 16 June 1915
Face brick on the tower replaced
Electricity installed; characteristic changed to a group of two flashes every six seconds (LF gives 1925 here and 1926 elsewhere)
Automated at the end of Jacox's tenure (LF)
Deactivated by the Coast Guard, 1 January 1954
Upper half of the brick tower removed because of structural damage
Coast Guard's replacement fifty-foot skeletal steel tower
Dwelling, thirty-foot tower, 4.7 acres and carriage house sold for $14,500 to private owners
Relit 28 February 1996 after Coast Guard approval (Wikipedia gives 1999; not cited)
Keeper's dwelling run as Braddock Point Bed & Breakfast, 2010 to 2020

corrections.why: The 1899 Board report records a lens change (270-degree lens replacing a 180-degree lens), not a new tower. The tower dates from 1895-96 (LHB 1895, 1896).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LF says the light was automated at the end of Jacox's tenure (about 1947), before the Coast Guard deactivated it on 1 January 1954. USLHS gives 1954 as the discontinued year. Both are reported in the story.

notes_for_editor: 1) Heights: USLHS 93 ft above MHW and 86 ft to the lantern; LF 97 ft original tower and 65 ft after the 1995 rebuild. The record's structure height (15.0 m) and focal height (17 m, about 55 ft) fit neither source read here; Wikipedia's lead gives 55 ft focal height, but it is not cited. Editor to decide. 2) Relight: LF gives 28 February 1996 (record's first_lit 1996 agrees); Wikipedia lead gives 28 February 1999 (not cited). Unresolved; the record keeps 1996. 3) Electrification year: LF gives 1925 in one passage and 1926 in another. The story avoids the year. 4) Characteristic: record's Iso W 6s is not confirmed by a source read here; LF says the 1925 change gave a group of two flashes every six seconds. Left as recorded. 5) Coordinates: record 43.3408, -77.762 (LF); USLHS 43 deg 20'28"N, 77 deg 45'52"W (about 43.3411, -77.7644). Minor difference; left as recorded. 6) Owners: the 1957 buyers, the 1986 owners and the 2008 owners who ran the bed and breakfast are not named, because they are private persons (the inn owners named in LF are not named here either). 7) Keepers: names, years and Coleman's birth and death years and salary come from the USLHS roster and keeper record (Kraig Anderson inventory); Jacox's jewelry business, Coleman's 1899 fall and his 700-mile estimate come from LF. Family details in LF are omitted. Roster matched to the record by roster.py (0.20 km, name and position). 8) Board reports are cited by corpus label and scan page; printed pages were not read. 9) The USLHS place page in the cache is short (1,129 characters); a 'Historical Information' passage seen in a search snippet could not be read from the cache and is not cited. 10) The USCG Historian's Braddock Point article (live site blocked; archive copy not readable) is not cited. 11) Wreck and rescue: no narrative for this station turned up. The LSS stranding table lists 'Braddocks Point' with OCR-scrambled figures; no counts used. 12) Lens: current optic removed (USLHS). Where the lens is now is not known from the sources read. 13) Page reads: about 9 (LF, USLHS place and person, Wikipedia lead, Lighthouse Board and Bulletin pages via corpus), plus 1 WebSearch and 3 newspaper searches (no usable hits). FACT-CHECK 2026-10-28: (a) The 1902 entry corrected: the main lens light was discontinued, not used; a lens-lantern light was shown (LF). (b) Life-Saving Service tables (1892-1900) list 'Braddocks Point' in the Lake Ontario table; the OCR scrambles the columns, so no counts are used and it is not known whether the entry is a station or a stranding location. (c) The 1896-1897 Light-House Board volume has no usable page index: item 1202 and the Cleveland entry are cited without scan pages. (d) The 1891-92 report says cession of jurisdiction had not yet been granted; the 1893 report says it was obtained under the May 1892 general law; both are cited.
